answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock a $100 bond for 90 days before it can bid on jobs, whether booking a terrace, buying cedar, or routing cargo through a harbor. Creating new keys is free, but activating 10,000 fake agents ties up $1 million for three months. The bond makes each additional identity consume scarce capital, so an attacker pays financing and opportunity costs even if every bond is eventually returned.
